Alex: Heads-up: rolling out two small but important changes to the release train workflow next cycle. Please skim and flag blockers.
Nora: quick TL;DR?
Alex: 1) Priority lanes: services can opt into high/normal/low lanes to control scheduling and capacity. 2) Autoscale prewarm: for high lane canaries we pre-allocate GPU workers for the first 10 minutes to avoid cold-start blips.
Chen: How do we opt a service into a lane?
Alex: Add priority_lane to your service manifest. Example: ```service_deploy:
  priority_lane: "high" # high|normal|low
  prewarm_workers: 2 # only used when priority_lane == high
  prewarm_duration: "10m"
```
Diego: Does high lane mean automatic bump in rollout speed? Any risk to safety checks?
Alex: No automatic speedup. High lane gets scheduling priority and prewarm. Rollout pacing still follows rollout_policy.ramp_steps and perf gates. Safety checks unchanged.
Priya: Note for PMs: releases that touch model shard/quantization must have perf signoff before hitting high lane. We'll block high lane requests without a perf artifacts link.
Nora: Can infra autoscale still reclaim prewarm workers early if cluster needs capacity?
Alex: Yes. Prewarm is best-effort. If cluster needs capacity, autoscaler may evict prewarm workers; we'll surface eviction events to the release UI.
Chen: Any monitoring changes?
Alex: We'll add a prewarm_worker metric and a canary_prewarm_evictions counter. Dashboards updated: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/deploy-prewarm
deploy-bot: FYI: next canary window for message-service is Wed 09:00 UTC (will honor new priority lanes).
Diego: If we opt into low lane, how long to wait for scheduling?
Alex: Low lane is backlog-scheduled; might shift to next Week B if capacity is tight. Do not use low lane for customer-facing hotfixes.
Priya: Process reminder: for hotpatches use the emergency-hotpatch flow (file emergency tag + link to rollback plan). Hotpatches bypass normal lane scheduling but still require an oncall ack.
Nora: Can we get a quick guardrail added to CI to ensure prewarm_workers is present for high lane services?
Chen: I'll add a lint rule that warns if priority_lane=="high" and prewarm_workers is missing.
Alex: Also small perf tweak: canary ramp pause added at 60% traffic for 5m when prewarm_workers > 0 to observe tail latencies. Please check your rollout_policy.
Diego: Example snippet to keep on hand?
Alex: Sure: ```rollout_policy:
  canary_duration: "30m"
  ramp_steps: ["10%","30%","60%","100%"]
  pause_at: "60%"
  pause_duration: "5m"
```
Priya: We'll publish a short runbook + the updated release-playbook section by EOD. Link will be posted here when live.
deploy-bot: Prewarm preview: service=message-service shard=us-east-1 prewarm_workers=2 prewarm_duration=10m
Nora: Thanks. When does this land?
Alex: Deploy cycle starting Monday. We'll run a pilot with infra-owned services on Friday. If you want to opt a service early, reply here with service name and owner.
Chen: Adding lint PR now.
Diego: I'll sync with PMs on the perf signoff requirement.
Priya: Invite for a 20m walkthrough tomorrow 09:30 UTC going out in a min. :calendar:
Alex: Thanks all — ping me or @Priya if this blocks anything. :thumbsup:
